summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload not declared in package files
details: The package declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` that downloads a Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases and uses that freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execute `math_init.js`, a 727KB heavily-obfuscated Bun-compiled JS blob shipped at the tarball root. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator-style `_0xXXXX` variable renaming and string-property dispatch tables; `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled bundle carrying a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header and a rotated numeric string-array decoder. The advertised purpose is a small CLI to gather version data, which has no legitimate need for an alternate JS runtime. Additionally, `package.json` sets `"files": ["src"]`, but both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` ship at the tarball root — the payload executed at install time is outside the author's declared file surface, consistent with a smuggled artifact from a compromised publish. Installing the package causes arbitrary code (the obfuscated Bun-bundled blob) to run on the installer's host under the downloaded Bun binary, evading Node-focused inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
